Feluda.description: The central detective protagonist known for his sharp intellect, whose real name is Pradosh C. Mitter.

Topshe.description: Feluda's younger cousin and loyal assistant, whose full name is Tapesh, and who serves as the story's narrator.

Kalikinkar Majumdar.description: An elderly man who invites Feluda to his mansion in Ghurghutia, and whose mysterious locked chest is central to the plot.

Gokul.description: The old and loyal servant of Kalikinkar Majumdar, who has served the family for thirty years.

Vishwanath Majumdar.description: Kalikinkar Majumdar's son from Calcutta, who disguised himself as the manager Rajen Babu and was revealed to be the murderer.

Monilal.description: The driver of Kalikinkar Majumdar, who drives Feluda and Topshe from the station.

Mr Sarkar.description: The sub-inspector at the local police station who assists Feluda in investigating the crime.

Ghurghutia.description: A village in Bengal where the story is set and Kalikinkar Majumdar's mansion is located.

Plassey.description: A town in Bengal, historically significant as the site of the Battle of Plassey in 1757.

Nadia.description: A district in West Bengal, India, where Ghurghutia and Plassey are located.

Sealdah.description: A major railway station in Kolkata, from where trains to Plassey depart.

Lalgola Passenger.description: A passenger train running between Sealdah and Lalgola, stopping at Plassey.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in India and home to Feluda and Vishwanath.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, encompassing West Bengal and Bangladesh.

palash.description: A type of tree (Butea monosperma) whose flowers are bright red and which gave Plassey its name.

Siraj-ud-daula.description: The last independent Nawab of Bengal, defeated at the Battle of Plassey.

Behrampore.description: A town in West Bengal, mentioned as a place to fetch doctors.

College Street.description: A famous street in Kolkata known for its many bookstores.

Ranaghat.description: A town in West Bengal, mentioned as a stop where Feluda and Topshe have tea and sweets.

Ambassador.description: A classic Indian car model, commonly used as taxis and by government officials.

Gaboriau.description: Refers to Émile Gaboriau, a French writer considered one of the pioneers of detective fiction.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment for men, consisting of a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

zamindar.description: A landowner, especially one who owned large estates in Bengal during the colonial period.

dacoits.description: Armed bandits or robbers, especially those operating in rural India.

naubatkhana.description: A music room or drum house, often found at the entrance of large Indian mansions or palaces.

namaskar.description: A traditional Indian greeting, similar to 'hello', often accompanied by folding the hands.

Babu.description: A respectful term of address for men, especially in Bengal.

Chhoto Babu.description: A term meaning 'younger gentleman' or 'young master', used to refer to the younger son in a Bengali household.

kurta.description: A loose, collarless shirt worn in South Asia.

daal.description: A dish made from lentils, a staple in Indian cuisine.
